Subject: Re: RFQ: reserved capacity options + GPU price sensitivity for Q4 launch

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the traffic estimates. I put together an initial commercial sketch and a sensitivity workbook (attached) that shows three pricing tiers with corresponding commit sizes and approval bands. High level:

- Base 12-month reserve (Tier A): 180–240 GPU-equivalent commitment — list rate with a 20% volume discount at sign.
- Extended commitment (Tier B): 240–360 — additional 8–12% discount but requires VP Sales signoff.
- Enterprise partner (Tier C): >360 or multi-year — custom pricing, needs CRO approval and finance hedge language.

Sensitivity approach: we modeled a GPU spot-cost shock of +/- 20% and applied a cost-pass-through clause that triggers at +/-10% sustained movement over a 30-day rolling window. The workbook includes two amortization options: (1) fixed monthly unit price with quarterly true-up; (2) CPI-like adjustment only for direct GPU price component.

I attached: gpu-price-sensitivity-v1.xlsx (model + narrative), and a short approval-stub template that outlines who needs to sign for each discount band.

Quick asks:
- Confirm Praxis's appetite for a pass-through (do you prefer hold-harmless vs. percentage pass-through?).
- Confirm expected ramp (you mentioned month-3 steady-state — is month-1 50% of that?)

If you want, I can route the finance approval request; Marissa is cc'd here. Happy to jump on a 30-min call Thu to walk the model.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: Praxis RFQ — recommended discount & price-protection language (internal)

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you both for quick review and sign-off path. Praxis has a realistic chance of signing by mid-Aug, but procurement is pushing for price-protection that could meaningfully move our margin if GPU costs spike. Summary of what I'm proposing (see attached model):

- Commercial: 12-month, 220-GPU equivalent commit; pricing at Tier A + 10% (so effectively list - 28% total vs list) — this is the offer I think we can win with minimal escalation.
- Protection: pass-through clause capped at +/- 12% per annum with a 30-day sustained trigger (only applies to the hardware-cost component).
- Cushion: allow a one-time 10% shortfall adjustment (in month-6 true-up) to accommodate slower ramp; any larger shortfall should convert to an agreed ramp-down schedule with penalty amortized over remaining months.

Approvals needed: Marissa (Finance) for the 28% effective discount; Karthik (Field Ops / Dedicated) to confirm feasibility of committing that fleet mix given current capacity plans and buffer requirements. If either recommends higher discount or special SLA, I'll escalate to VP Sales.

I'm marking this urgent — Praxis needs the final commercial doc by Mon 8/9 for their CFO review.

Thanks,
Sean

(Attached: gpu-price-sensitivity-v1.xlsx; approval-stub-sept_tranche.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Praxis RFQ — recommended discount & price-protection language (internal)

Sean / Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and workbook. Read-through notes and recommended redlines below (finance perspective):

1) Discount band: approving an effective ~28% off list for a 12-month commit of ~220 GPUs is acceptable provided Praxis signs the standard non‑reducible tranche on months 1–3 (i.e., first 3 months billed in full regardless of usage). This reduces our downside risk.

2) Price-protection: prefer a hybrid pass-through — 70% of GPU spot delta beyond a 10% threshold flows to the customer, 30% absorbed by Redwood, capped at 12% annual moved amount. Rationale: shares risk while keeping commercial simplicity.

3) Shortfall mechanics: allow the one-time 10% soft adjustment at month-6. Any further reduction should convert into a 60-day ramp-down notice with the remaining committed GPU months paid at a 50% discount to encourage re-commit or early termination buyout.

4) Approval path: Finance approves the 28% effective discount under these guardrails. Anything deeper (>=35% effective) must go to the CFO and require a compensating clause (e.g., minimum annualized commitment in dollars or multi-year).

5) Ops constraints: Karthik, please confirm if 220-GPU equivalent can be provisioned from our reserved pool without impacting other enterprise commitments. If not, we should present Praxis with a staggered delivery schedule tied to tranche payments.

If Karthik signs off operationally, I'm fine to authorize Sean to present these terms to Praxis and start contract prep. I've attached a draft approval-stub that Praxis can sign to speed the process.

—Marissa
Director, Finance (Revenue) | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
